questions.q: Insoluble means cannot dissolve. Describe what digestion does to large, insoluble food molecules.
questions.explain: Digestion breaks large, insoluble food molecules into small, soluble molecules. Small, soluble molecules can be absorbed into the blood.

questions.q: Our body uses food for energy, growth and repair. Explain why food must be digested.
choices: so it can enter the blood
so it can leave as faeces
questions.explain: Only small, soluble molecules can pass into the blood. So food must be digested before the body can absorb and use it.

questions.q: Teeth cut food into smaller pieces. Identify the type of digestion.
questions.explain: Cutting food into smaller pieces does not change the food into new substances. This is physical digestion.

questions.q: Enzymes break food down into simpler substances. Identify the type of digestion.
questions.explain: Enzymes break food down into simpler substances, which changes what the food is made of. This is chemical digestion.

questions.q: Bile is a liquid that acts on fats. Describe what bile does to fats.
choices: breaks big droplets into small ones
questions.explain: Bile breaks big fat droplets into many small droplets. This gives enzymes a larger surface to work on. Bile does not digest fat itself.

questions.q: The alimentary canal is the food tube. Name the part where food enters it.
questions.explain: Food enters the alimentary canal at the mouth.

questions.q: The gullet joins the mouth to the stomach. Describe how it moves food.
choices: contracts and relaxes to push food
questions.explain: The muscles in the wall of the gullet contract and relax in waves. This squeezes and pushes the food down to the stomach.

questions.q: The stomach makes acid. State the function of this acid.
questions.explain: The acid in the stomach kills most bacteria in the food. It also gives the stomach enzymes the acidic conditions they work best in.

questions.q: Food has just left the stomach. Name the part it enters next.
questions.explain: Food leaves the stomach and enters the small intestine.

questions.q: Name the part of the alimentary canal where digested food is absorbed.
questions.explain: Digested food is absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.

questions.q: State the function of the large intestine.
questions.explain: The large intestine absorbs water and mineral salts from the undigested food. Digested food is absorbed in the small intestine, and faeces are stored in the rectum.

questions.q: Faeces is undigested food. Name the part that stores faeces before it leaves.
questions.explain: Faeces are stored in the rectum. They leave the body through the anus.

questions.q: Bile is a greenish-yellow liquid. Name the organ that produces bile.
questions.explain: Bile is made in the liver. It is stored in the gall bladder.

questions.q: Bile is made in the liver. State the function of the gall bladder.
questions.explain: The gall bladder stores bile. The bile is made in the liver.

questions.q: Name the organ that breaks down alcohol into harmless substances.
questions.explain: The liver breaks down alcohol into harmless substances.

questions.q: Name the organ that stores extra glucose in the body.
questions.explain: The liver stores extra glucose (as glycogen). It releases it again when the body needs it.

questions.q: Insulin controls glucose in the blood. Name the organ that produces insulin.
questions.explain: The pancreas makes insulin. Insulin controls the amount of glucose in the blood.

questions.q: Enzymes speed up digestion. Name the enzyme that digests proteins.
questions.explain: Protease is the enzyme that digests proteins. Lipase digests fats and carbohydrase digests carbohydrates.

questions.q: Enzymes speed up digestion. Name the enzyme that digests fats.
questions.explain: Lipase is the enzyme that digests fats. Bile breaks fats into droplets but is not an enzyme.

questions.q: Carbohydrase is an enzyme. Name the nutrient that carbohydrase digests.
questions.explain: Carbohydrase digests carbohydrates, such as starch, into sugars.

questions.q: Saliva is made by the salivary glands. Name the enzyme in saliva.
questions.explain: Saliva contains carbohydrase. It starts to digest starch in the mouth.

questions.q: The stomach makes a digestive juice. Name the enzyme in this juice.
questions.explain: The stomach makes a digestive juice with protease, which starts to digest proteins.

questions.q: Name the organ that produces carbohydrase, protease and lipase.
questions.explain: The pancreas makes a juice with all three enzymes, carbohydrase, protease and lipase. The juice flows into the small intestine.

questions.q: State the temperature at which enzymes in our body work best.
questions.explain: Enzymes in our body work best at body temperature, which is about 37 °C.

questions.q: A digestive enzyme is heated to 80 °C. Predict what happens to the enzyme.
questions.explain: A high temperature such as 80 °C destroys the enzyme. It cannot work again, even when cooled.

questions.q: A digestive enzyme is kept at a low temperature. Predict what happens to the enzyme.
questions.explain: At a low temperature the enzyme becomes inactive and works very slowly. It is not destroyed and works again when warmed.

questions.q: An enzyme digests food in the shortest time at 35 °C. State its optimum temperature.
questions.explain: The optimum temperature is the temperature at which an enzyme works best. This enzyme digests food fastest at 35 °C, so that is its optimum temperature.

questions.q: Stomach enzymes work in acid. State the pH at which they work best.
questions.explain: The stomach is acidic. Stomach enzymes work best at about pH 2.

questions.q: State the pH at which enzymes in the small intestine work best.
questions.explain: The small intestine is slightly alkaline. Its enzymes work best at about pH 8.

questions.q: State the pH at which enzymes in the mouth work best.
questions.explain: Saliva is about neutral. Enzymes in the mouth work best at about pH 7.

questions.q: A digestive enzyme works best at pH 2. Identify where in the body it works.
questions.explain: pH 2 is acidic. The stomach is the acidic part of the alimentary canal, so the enzyme works there.

questions.q: A digestive enzyme works best at pH 8. Identify where in the body it works.
questions.explain: pH 8 is slightly alkaline. The small intestine is slightly alkaline, so the enzyme works there.

questions.q: A person drinks too much alcohol for many years. Name a disease this can cause.
questions.explain: Drinking too much alcohol for many years damages the liver. It can cause liver cancer.

questions.q: A diet lacks fibre and water. Name the problem this causes.
questions.explain: Fibre and water help food move through the gut. Without enough of them, the faeces become hard and constipation results.

questions.q: In diabetes, a substance in the blood cannot be controlled. Name the substance.
questions.explain: In diabetes the body cannot control the amount of glucose in the blood.

questions.q: A doctor checks a patient for diabetes. State what the doctor measures.
questions.explain: Diabetes is a problem with controlling blood sugar. So the doctor measures the sugar (glucose) level in the blood.

questions.q: A diet high in two nutrients can lead to diabetes. Name the two nutrients.
questions.explain: A diet high in fat and sugar can lead to obesity and diabetes.
